swap.evidence: Products: a GP surgery appointment booker and a council parking-permit form. Surviving unchanged: white header with name in bold body text, pale blue-grey ground, single native-control column, navy rectangular button, red error summary, label/value summary list, white footer band with phone number. Bound to this product: the anchor glyph, the tide-times table content, berth copy ('Afloat at every state of the tide'), 'Draught' and 'MMSI' fields. category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a small public/municipal booking flow: government-style form pattern, humanist sans, light ground, navy or teal primary button, red error summary, summary list. Predicted opposite: a nautical costume (navy and white stripes, rope, chart textures). Every identity-carrying element matches the default; it avoids the opposite only by having no harbour reference at all.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online pitch booking for a small tidal-island campsite, phones, outdoor light'. Predicted choices: single-column native form, one dark accent button, plain data table for crossing times, cards with radio buttons, error summary. Overlap is complete; nothing in the render was driven specifically by the sill gate or the harbour.

findings.title: Sterile default: no identity or signature on any surface beyond the name and an anchor glyph
findings.description: Every route uses the same frame: white header with 'Saltmarsh Quay' in bold body-size text and a small anchor glyph, pale blue-grey ground, a single column of native controls, one navy button, white footer band. No imagery, no drawn device, no typographic moment, no colour role taken from the harbour's world. The frame passes for any small public-service booking form.
findings.impact: Returning and new skippers may not recognise the booking as the harbour's own, and the page is likely to read as unfinished to its audience; the brief's one distinguishing mechanism (the sill gate and tide) contributes nothing visible.
findings.recommendation: Write the missing DESIGN.md first: decide attributes and an identity floor taken from the harbour's own world, and choose one signature that comes from the tide/sill-gate mechanism, appearing quietly across the steps. Keep the conventional Operate structure.

findings.title: The tide window, the product's distinguishing mechanism, is a detached generic table below the form
findings.description: On / the 'Arrival time' select offers 'Choose a time' with no visible relation to the sill-gate window; the high-water table sits below the button as a plain white table, with the gate rule ('open from about two hours before high water until two hours after') as small grey caption text. The reader must compute the window themselves. The table is also labelled 'times in UTC' while the brief specifies local times.
findings.impact: Skippers on a phone may have to scroll past the submit button to work out the gate window and then convert UTC to local time (BST applies on 17 October), which can lead to an arrival time outside the gate. It is also the obvious place for the product's signature and it is unused.

evidence.detail: 'High water at the quay, times in UTC'; context.md: '24-hour times in local time'

findings.recommendation: Decide how the gate window is shown at the point of choosing the arrival time, in local time, so the tide shapes the step rather than sitting under it.

findings.title: Tide-table column headers left-aligned over right-aligned times
findings.description: 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' headers start at the left of their columns while the times sit flush right, so each header floats ~80-130px left of its figures at 1280 and the Afternoon header sits nearer the morning times.
findings.impact: A skipper scanning for the afternoon high water may read the wrong column, especially at a glance in bright light.
findings.recommendation: Align numeric column headers with their figures.

findings.title: Isolated overflow '...' button hides 'Change dates' outside the content column
findings.description: On /berths.html a bordered '...' button sits alone in an empty row at the far right (x~1028-1072 at 1280), beyond the card column (ends ~752) and past the header nav's right edge. It holds 'Change dates' and 'Harbour rules'. It is the third fixation on the page and carries no label.
findings.impact: Changing the arrival date is a core task; hiding it behind an unlabelled glyph may make it hard to find, and the stray control breaks the page's single-column alignment, adding an empty band above the list.
findings.recommendation: Decide where the stay summary and its change action live so they sit in the content column and are visible without a menu.

findings.title: Footer band stops short on short pages, leaving a flat empty band at wide widths
findings.description: On boat, review, confirmed and the booking-stopped state at 1280, the white footer ends mid-viewport (y~295-830) and the remainder of the viewport is flat page ground.
findings.impact: The page looks unfinished at desktop widths, most visibly on the confirmation, the moment the skipper decides whether to trust the booking.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages fill the viewport so the footer sits at the bottom or the ground continues consistently.

findings.title: Browser-default date control shows 'yyyy/mm/dd' against the brief's date format
findings.description: The Arrival date input renders the unthemed browser placeholder 'yyyy/mm/dd' with the system calendar glyph at every width, while the rest of the flow writes dates as 'Saturday 17 October 2026'.
findings.impact: The first control on the first step is a visible browser default, a sign of unfinish, and its format conflicts with the en-GB date format the rest of the product uses, which may cause hesitation for older skippers.
findings.recommendation: Decide on a date entry pattern whose displayed format matches the product's en-GB date format.

findings.title: Length input keeps a neutral border in the error state while other errored fields turn red
findings.description: In boat/errors, 'Enter the length' is shown, but the Length input border is dark, while Boat name, Draught and MMSI inputs have red borders.
findings.impact: Inconsistent error marking may make the Length field look valid when scanning the form, and it is the field that decides whether the boat fits.
findings.recommendation: Apply one error treatment to every errored field.

findings.title: Confirmation omits the arrival time and gives the reference no emphasis
findings.description: 'Booking confirmed' shows the reference SQ-1017-C3 in bold body text and lists Arrival as 'Saturday 17 October 2026' without the 15:00 time that the review page showed.
findings.impact: The two facts a skipper needs on arrival, the reference and the gate-bound arrival time, are respectively under-weighted and missing on the page they are likely to screenshot.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the confirmation's focal point is and include the arrival time.

findings.title: 'Booking stopped' is a dead end with no explanation or route forward
findings.description: The length-over-limit state replaces the page with 'Booking stopped / This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' No reason, no link back to choose a larger berth (the wall berth takes up to 15 m), no call-to-office prompt beyond the generic footer.
findings.impact: A skipper whose boat is too long for the chosen pontoon may abandon the booking although a wall berth fits; the bare page also reads as an error screen rather than part of the product.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the skipper should do next when the boat does not fit and show that path on this state.

findings.title: Heading 'Choose a pontoon space' does not match a list that includes a wall berth
findings.description: The H1 and the group label 'Pontoon spaces free on these dates' cover four options, the fourth of which is 'Wall berth 2 — Settles on soft mud at low water'.
findings.impact: Skippers with boats over 12 m, who must use the wall berth, may think the page has no option for them before reaching the last card.
findings.recommendation: Use one term for the full set of berths on offer.

findings.title: One-word last lines in headings and hints at 320-375
findings.description: At narrow widths several strings end with a single stranded word: H1 'Choose a pontoon space' ('space'), H1 'Check your mooring booking' ('booking'), harbour rules ('walls.', 'berth.'), draught hint ('float'), mobile hint ('change').
findings.impact: Stranded words on the H1s are the most visible, adding to the unfinished look on phones, the primary device.
findings.recommendation: Balance heading wraps at narrow widths.

_strengths: Copy is in the skippers' own words and matter-of-fact: 'Afloat at every state of the tide', 'Settles on soft mud at low water', 'The harbour office sends a text if the gate times change'.
Conventional, calm Operate structure: one primary action per step, standard error summary with linked messages, clear label/value review list; holds at 320 without breakage.
High-contrast dark text on a light ground suits bright-cockpit use.
_keep: Keep the plain, specific copy and the one-action-per-step structure; any identity added must not cost contrast or the conventional controls.
notes: No baseline/ in packet, so pairwise not run (DES-05 not_applicable). design.md is missing, so brand fit is not assessable and DEC-02 is not met; rubric brand_fit score 0 is a schema placeholder meaning n/a. No dark-theme captures; forced-colors and more-contrast variants exist but were not used for design judgement. Detector file was opened only after critic-3.verdict.json was written.
